summary: Microsoft Corp. has acquired 124 acres of land in Gainesville, Virginia, for over $465 million, intending to build data centers. summary: The music industry is experiencing a resurgence fueled by "funflation" (increased spending on live events) and technological advancements such as streaming, AI, and blockchain. These initiatives, announced after better-than-expected Q4 results, demonstrate Target's commitment to brick-and-mortar growth and customer loyalty through improved shopping experiences and supply chain efficiency.

This move follows a liquidity crisis for The Body Shop Canada, which owes approximately CA$3.3 million in overdue debt, including CA$900,000 to landlords, and has led to significant job cuts. The Canadian operation's reliance on its U.S. counterpart for distribution and e-commerce, which has now stopped, further complicated its situation.

summary: The Sonos Era 100 is a revamped smart speaker offering significant improvements over its predecessors like the Sonos One. It provides impressive, room-filling sound quality with enhanced stereo separation and a larger woofer. Notable new features include Bluetooth support and a USB-C port for line-in audio, making it versatile despite lacking Google Assistant and certain Trueplay advanced tuning for Android users.

title: Veritone launches AI-powered digital evidence management system
summary: Veritone has launched its new AI-powered Intelligent Digital Evidence Management System (iDEMS) to modernize digital evidence management for public safety and judicial agencies. The system extracts valuable data, automates workflows from data silos into a secure, centralized AI-driven platform, and integrates with leading industry software. Built on Veritone’s aiWARE and hosted on AWS, iDEMS centralizes digital evidence, streamlines redaction, improves analysis, and tracks persons of interest across various media types.

title: AT&T agrees to purchase carbon credits from Occidental's 1PointFive
summary: AT&T has agreed to purchase carbon dioxide removal credits from Occidental's 1PointFive as part of its goal to achieve carbon neutrality by 2035. The credits will come from 1PointFive's Stratos direct air capture facility currently under construction in Texas, which is designed to capture up to 500,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide annually. This agreement follows similar deals 1PointFive has made with other major companies like Amazon.

Investors are closely watching the $206.22 level, which represents IBM's all-time high, as a potential resistance point for the stock.

title: Eli Lilly partners with Amazon to deliver GLP-1 drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound
summary: Eli Lilly has partnered with Amazon to distribute its GLP-1 drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound, along with migraine medications, through LillyDirect and Amazon Pharmacy. This collaboration aims to improve patient access amid high demand and shortages for Lilly's popular GLP-1 drugs, which significantly boosted the company's recent quarterly revenue to $2.5 billion. The initiative further solidifies Amazon's presence in the healthcare sector, following previous ventures into prescription drug delivery and diabetes care.

title: Eli Lilly taps Amazon Pharmacy to help deliver weight loss drug Zepbound, other medicines to patients
summary: Eli Lilly has partnered with Amazon Pharmacy to facilitate the home delivery of prescription drugs, including the weight loss medication Zepbound, through its direct-to-consumer website, LillyDirect. This collaboration aims to enhance patient access by providing two-day delivery for Amazon Prime members and offering 24/7 access to clinical pharmacists. The move reflects efforts to streamline drug distribution and reduce consumer costs, especially as demand for Zepbound and similar drugs continues to soar.

title: Microsoft, P&G, Unilever and Walmart among 239 companies to miss net-zero deadline
summary: The Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) has reclassified 239 companies, including Microsoft, P&G, Unilever, and Walmart, as "commitment removed" for net-zero goals because they failed to submit science-based targets for validation within the 24-month deadline. A significant obstacle for these companies is the difficulty in reducing Scope 3 emissions, which relate to indirect emissions from customers and supply chains. Despite the reclassification, these major corporations maintain that they are continuing to pursue aggressive emissions reduction targets and are in various stages of reviewing or updating their strategies to align with SBTi standards, with many still holding near-term validated targets.

title: Oracle unveils $10B data center expansion plan
summary: Oracle announced plans to spend $10 billion in 2025 to expand its data center capacity due to exceptionally high demand for its cloud network. CEO Safra Catz and CTO Larry Ellison highlighted the scale of these new facilities, with one U.S. AI data center capable of housing eight Boeing 747s. This expansion positions Oracle alongside other tech giants in hyperscaler data center construction, despite ongoing industry challenges like supply chain issues and lengthened buildout timelines.

This marks a significant accessibility improvement for pregnancy prevention, especially for those who face barriers to seeing a healthcare provider.

summary: A new report indicates a significant shift in Canadian television viewing habits towards streaming platforms and away from traditional cable and satellite. By the end of 2023, 42% of Canadian households had no traditional TV subscription, a figure expected to reach 50% by 2026. Conversely, over 80% of households subscribe to a streaming service, with streaming revenue increasing while traditional TV revenue declined, prompting calls for regulatory changes from Canadian broadcasters to level the playing field.

title: S&P Global Commodity Insights and Amazon Web Services Empower Digital Transformation in Upstream Oil & Gas Industry
summary: S&P Global Commodity Insights and Amazon Web Services (AWS) are collaborating to accelerate digital transformation in the upstream oil and gas industry. This partnership will provide energy companies with access to comprehensive upstream data on AWS Data Exchange and facilitate the development of cloud-based AI and machine learning tools, as well as access to S&P Global Commodity Insights' Kingdom™ Geoscience Software. The initiative aims to enhance decision-making, efficiency, and data interoperability for energy companies, supporting both traditional operations and the energy transition.

title: DWS social fairness SDG ETF: Screened rather than thematic impact
summary: DWS has launched the Xtrackers MSCI Global SDGs Social Fairness Contributors UCITS ETF (XDGS) which targets social fairness SDGs. While the ETF uses broad screening criteria to identify companies with positive contributions to social fairness, some experts question if it truly achieves "impact" by focusing on large companies in socially relevant sectors rather than those directly addressing social good for underserved populations. The article highlights that active management might be better suited for genuine impact investing in social SDGs.

title: POET Enters Optical Module Market with 800G Transceiver for Artificial Intelligence Networks
summary: POET Technologies Inc. announced its entry into the optical module market with the Wavelight™, an 800G pluggable transceiver designed for artificial intelligence and cloud data centers. This marks a significant commercial milestone for the company, showcasing its POET Optical Interposer™ technology. The Wavelight modules will be debuted at OFC 2024, with customer sampling beginning in Q3 2024, targeting a rapidly growing market for high-speed transceivers.

title: News | Amazon's HQ2 Takes Shape at Metropolitan Park
summary: Amazon's HQ2 in Arlington, Virginia, is taking shape with the opening of Metropolitan Park, the first phase of its sprawling redevelopment. This project, recognized with a CoStar Impact Award, includes two 22-story office towers, retail, and public spaces designed with sustainability in mind. Judges lauded the development for its positive impact on the community, cutting-edge architecture, and the creation of new jobs and amenities.

title: Proven Retail Winners: IKEA, Williams Sonoma, Crate + Barrel
summary: This article analyzes the performance of home furnishings retailers, identifying IKEA, Williams Sonoma, and Crate & Barrel as proven winners demonstrating adaptability and strong brand attributes despite economic challenges. It contrasts their success with Wayfair, which is presented as a potential loser due to operational challenges, declining revenue, and lack of brand differentiation. The article highlights how the successful companies have leveraged unified commerce, design differentiation, and solution-based selling to thrive.

title: A new product allows 5x leveraged bets on the Magnificent Seven. Traders should be wary.
summary: A new exchange-traded product allows investors to make 5x leveraged bets on the Magnificent Seven group of stocks, raising concerns among analysts. While levered exchange-traded products are gaining popularity, traders are warned about the significant risks associated with such highly leveraged instruments. ETF analyst Todd Sohn from Strategas Securities notes that this product appears to be the most heavily levered available in any developed market.

title: PREORDER! Transformers X Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Party Wallop Official Images & Details
summary: Hasbro has officially revealed the new Transformers x Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Party Wallop figure, available for preorder at $49.99. This unique collaborative figure transforms from the iconic TMNT Party Wagon into a robot and includes four swappable heads, allowing collectors to customize it to represent Donatello, Michelangelo, Leonardo, or Raphael. The figure is set to be released on July 21, 2024, and comes with various ninja weapon accessories.

title: This Is How Much Money Amazon Makes Every Minute
summary: Amazon, a colossal conglomerate that started as an online bookseller, generated nearly $575 billion in revenue last year, making an average of $1,093,588.28 per minute. After accounting for expenses, the company's net income for 2023 was $30.43 billion, translating to $57,886.23 in profit every minute. Amazon's stock has seen remarkable growth since its early days, with shares trading near all-time highs and benefiting from strong analyst recommendations.
